claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my child. His name is Alex and he's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex. Let me ask a few more questions to assess your eligibility.

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now, regarding Alex:

Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upkeep (for example, on food, clothes, or pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you.

One final question: Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or residential accommodation, or has he been in any of these for an extended period?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, actually Alex has been in hospital for a while now - he's been there for about three months or so.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex's hospital stay. Since Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks (about 3 months), there's an important exception that could still allow you to receive Child Benefit.

Do you regularly spend money on Alex while he's in hospital? This could include things like bringing him clothes, toys, food, or other items he needs.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, unfortunately I haven't been able to afford to spend money on his needs while he's in there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about your situation. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- You live in the UK
- Alex is 8 years old and normally lives with you
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- However, Alex has been in hospital for about 3 months (more than 12 weeks)
- You are not regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital

Unfortunately, the rules state that Child Benefit payments are affected when a child is in hospital for more than 12 weeks. An exception can apply if you regularly spend money on the child during their hospital stay, but since you've indicated you haven't been able to do this, the exception would not apply in your case.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, I'm sorry to say that **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Here's why:**

While you would normally qualify for Child Benefit because you live in the UK and Alex (aged 8) lives with you, the extended hospital stay affects your eligibility. The rules state that Child Benefit is usually stopped after a child has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks. Since Alex has been in hospital for approximately 3 months, this threshold has been exceeded.

There is an exception that could allow you to continue receiving Child Benefit if you regularly spend money on Alex while he's in hospital. However, since you've mentioned you haven't been able to afford to do this, this exception doesn't apply in your situation.

**What you can do:**

- If your circumstances change and you begin regularly spending money on Alex in hospital, you may become eligible again. I'd recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office to discuss your situation.
- Once Alex leaves hospital and returns home, you should be able to claim Child Benefit again. You would need to contact HMRC to restart your claim.

I understand this isn't the news you were hoping for, and I'm sorry about the difficult situation. If you have any other questions, please feel free to ask.
